messages:
juan_customer: Hey team — high priority. Our SSO-provisioned org key started returning 403 only for embeddings and rerank calls around ~1:05pm. Generation (text-complete) still works. This started right after we updated Okta entitlements for the group.

juan_customer: Repro steps I ran locally:
```bash
# using the org service key from SSO provisioning
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ORG_KEY'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"input": "test"}'
```

juan_customer: Response: 403 with body:
```json
{"error": "insufficient_scope", "message": "missing: embeddings"}
```

juan_customer: Note: same key successfully returns a generation response: `curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ORG_KEY'` — so it's definitely scope-related not a global revocation. Help? :eyes:

marie_cs: thanks for the repro, juan. Can you paste a request-id from the 403 response or the x-request-id header? Also which org-id and user email on the SSO side so we can correlate with the provisioner logs.

juan_customer: request-id: r-0a1b2c3d, org-id: org-789, sso user: juan@acme.co. I can also share the raw headers if helpful.

alex_eng: quick hypothesis — we've seen a few cases where the SSO provisioning job updates user entitlements in Okta but the internal "auth-store" used by the token minting service lags because the async sync job gets queued. That results in newly minted or reissued keys lacking freshly-added scopes for a short window. Can you confirm if the key was created/rotated after the Okta change?

juan_customer: yes rotated the service key ~5 minutes after the Okta update.

alex_eng: that fits. Two follow-ups: 1) check the token metadata header when you hit the API — we log `x-auth-scopes` at the edge. If your request lacks `embeddings` and `rerank` in that header, the token wasn't minted with those scopes. 2) workaround: run a force-sync or issue a short-lived admin sync; I'll paste the internal endpoint.

alex_eng: admin sync (internal):
```bash
curl -X POST https://provisioner.internal.redwood/v1/sync/orgs/org-789
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_OPS_TOKEN"
```

alex_eng: after that, re-mint the key or rotate the service key and try again. If that fixes it, we'll file a bug for more visible provisioning state in the UI.

sam_support: to add, if you're blocked in prod we can temporarily issue a scoped service key for embeddings/rerank while the sync finishes. It's a short-term fix but less disruptive than rolling your entire rotation. Ping me if you want us to create one (we'll need approval from your security contact). :thumbsup:

juan_customer: ran `curl -I` against the embed request to inspect headers — shows `x-auth-scopes: generate` only. So confirmed token mint didn't include embeddings.

alex_eng: ok that nails it. I'll trigger the sync and watch the queue. provisioner-bot should post status.

provisioner-bot: [provisioner] enqueue sync for org-789 by alex_eng — job id sync-4421.

provisioner-bot: [provisioner] job sync-4421 started.

provisioner-bot: [provisioner] job sync-4421 completed: 12 updated principals, 1 stale mapping removed.

alex_eng: done. Juan, can you re-issue the key (or mint a new one) and re-check `x-auth-scopes`?

juan_customer: re-minted new key and re-ran the curl. Now `x-auth-scopes: generate, embeddings, rerank`. Embeddings call returns 200. All good on our side. Thanks!

marie_cs: filing an internal follow-up ticket: CS-4982 — "SSO provisioning propagation delay leads to incomplete token scopes after rotation". We'll add mitigation: short-lived admin sync endpoint and doc note for rotations.

alex_eng: action items: (1) add a UI flag showing last successful provisioner sync per org; (2) add a reconcile job alarm when rotations occur within X minutes of Okta changes; (3) improve docs for customers to wait or trigger sync after entitlement changes.

juan_customer: appreciate the fast help team. Leaving this thread open until CS-4982 closes. :rocket:
